Summary: CAPITAL for private SEC filers: the issuer's Form D offering as a dated, issuer-bound observation (D6), quoted as stated, no counterparty inferred
Description: 1) Original intent: a private SEC filer that resolves by its Form D has no observation bound to it, so its packet reports 'no observations bound' even though its own Form D states a dated offering. The Founder ratified D6 (2026-10-12): admit the offering narrowly as a dated, issuer-bound CAPITAL observation, quoting disclosed amounts as stated, not inferring an undisclosed counterparty and not treating the offering alone as proof of a financing relationship. 2) Acceptance criteria: (a) one CAPITAL observation per newest Form D, bound to the subject by canonical id, dated by the filing, carrying the accession; (b) date of first sale, total offering amount, amount sold, remaining, investors already invested, security types and exemption quoted as the Form D states them; nothing computed; (c) the signal value does not depend on the amount (it follows the 8-K Item 3.02 equity-offering precedent); (d) the page states that the Form D names no investors and that the offering alone is not a financing relationship; (e) it is an observation, never a relationship, and creates none; (f) tests over real Form D documents; re-scoring of PC03 and PC04 before any claim. 3) Current implementation state: built and verified 2026-10-13: parse, packet, pool and page lines (qa_formd_offering 13/13); PC01 to PC04 each score 8.0. 4) Dependencies: KRYL-1412 (Form D identity), KRYL-1413 (Form D people). 5) Superseded: no. 6) Maps to the product model: yes (CAPITAL, evidence-bound). Not counted as coverage beyond the observation it is.
